sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia articles and publicly documented sources. Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya at 1496m, in the East Khasi Hills. Best season Oct–Jun; Jul–Sep is heavy monsoon. Mawphlang and Laitlum are ~23–24km from Shillong center — standard half-day excursions with no closer owning destination. All records needs_review.

places.name: Elephant Falls
places.description: Three-tier waterfall in the Upper Shillong area, 12km from the city centre. The 'elephant rock' that gave the falls their name was destroyed in the 1897 earthquake; the Khasi name Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew means 'three-step waterfall'. Each tier has a distinct character — the upper tier is narrow, the middle broad, the lower viewable from a path. Government-maintained park with entry fee. Stairway connecting all tiers; lower tier can be muddy after rain.

places.name: Ward's Lake
places.description: Horseshoe-shaped artificial lake at the heart of Shillong, built during British administration (1894–1900) and named after Chief Commissioner William Ward. Surrounded by a botanical garden with ornamental flower beds and walking paths. Pedal boats and rowboats available for hire. A popular morning-walk and picnic site for residents. The garden borders the Secretariat. Entry fee applies; boating charged separately.

places.name: Shillong Peak
places.description: Highest point near Shillong at 1961m, 10km south of the city, managed by the Indian Air Force. On clear days the panorama extends to Bangladesh plains on one side and to the Khasi Hills on the other. Civilian access is restricted to a designated viewpoint operated by the IAF (photography from the viewpoint is permitted; the core zone is off-limits). Entry permit required; Indian nationals with valid ID only. Timing and access subject to IAF operational requirements.
places.openingDays: Daily approx 09:00–16:00 (subject to IAF; closed on certain days)

places.name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
places.description: Seven-storey museum dedicated to the indigenous cultures of Northeast India and neighbouring regions, housed in a striking contemporary building in Mawlai, Shillong. Covers 18 states and territories; galleries display textiles, musical instruments, weapons, ritual objects, oral histories, and photographs documenting tribal traditions from Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya, and beyond. One of the most comprehensive tribal-culture museums in the region. Rooftop Sky Walk provides a 360° view of Shillong. Entry fee applies. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Umiam Lake
places.description: Large reservoir 15km north of Shillong on the Guwahati–Shillong highway, created by the Umiam-Umtru hydro project. Surrounded by pine-forested hills; the lakeside road offers panoramic views. The Meghalaya government-run Water Sports Complex offers motor-boating, kayaking, and angling (seasonal). The drive through the Barapani area at dawn or dusk is scenic in itself. A popular half-day escape from Shillong. Best season Oct–May; avoid during monsoon when visibility is poor.
places.openingDays: Lake viewable year-round; Water Sports Complex seasonal (approx Oct–May)

places.name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
places.description: Ancient sacred Khasi forest (Law Lyngdoh) at Mawphlang village, 23km south of Shillong. Protected by Khasi customary law for over 1000 years — no plant, flower, stone or soil may be taken from the grove. Guided visits only; guides are appointed by the village Syiem (chief). The 78-hectare grove is a rare old-growth forest containing many species lost from surrounding hills. Monoliths and stone memorials to Khasi ancestors are scattered through the trees. A profound cultural and ecological experience.

places.name: Laitlum Canyons
places.description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint in the East Khasi Hills, 22km from Shillong near Smit village. 'Laitlum' means 'end of the hills' in Khasi. The plateau-edge viewpoint drops away into a deep valley of layered sandstone and forest — a striking landscape of narrow gorges and mist-filled depths. The gorge and terraced farmland in the valley below are photogenic in any weather. A steep path descends into the canyon for those who want to explore further. Best at dawn or in light mist.

places.name: Cathedral of Mary Help of Christians
places.description: Catholic cathedral at the heart of Shillong, seat of the Archdiocese of Shillong. One of the most prominent religious buildings in Northeast India, built in an Italian Gothic style with twin spires. The surrounding area (Laitumkhrah) is the Christian quarter of the city and Shillong has one of the highest concentrations of Christians in India (~74% of Meghalaya's population). Free to enter outside service times.
places.openingDays: Daily 07:00–19:00 (access may be restricted during services)

places.name: Shillong Golf Course
places.description: 18-hole natural golf course established in 1898 by British officers, among the oldest natural grass courses in Asia and sometimes cited as the oldest in the region. Set in the heart of Shillong at 1500m altitude, the course is surrounded by pine trees and open to visitors for day golf (with caddie hire). The adjacent Polo Ground is the venue for Shillong's winter football and polo season. Non-golfers can walk the pine-tree boundary. Entry for golf is paid; the surrounding area is free to view.
places.openingDays: Daily 06:00–18:00 (fee for golf; viewing area free)

places.name: Lady Hydari Park
places.description: Government-maintained botanical garden and mini-zoo in the heart of Shillong, named after Lady Hydari (wife of the first Governor of Assam). The garden has lawns, flowerbeds, and a greenhouse. The small zoo section houses deer, porcupines, clouded leopard, and several Northeast bird species. A gentle family-friendly half-day outing near the city centre. Entry fee applies; zoo section included.

places.name: State Museum of Meghalaya
places.description: Archaeological and cultural museum maintained by the Meghalaya government, displaying tribal artefacts, traditional Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo costumes, jewellery, musical instruments, and historical documents. A compact but well-organised collection introducing the distinct cultures of Meghalaya's three tribal peoples. Located near the Secretariat building in central Shillong. Nominal entry fee; closed Mondays.

places.name: Nohwet Rock, Mawkdok Valley
places.description: Dramatic valley viewpoint on the Shillong–Sohra highway, 28km south of Shillong and 23km north of Sohra. The Mawkdok Dympep Valley offers a sudden, vertiginous panorama of the Khasi escarpment — green terraced hillsides dropping to a valley floor. A zip-line (flying fox) operated by a private concession runs across part of the valley; one of the few commercial adventure activities on the Meghalaya plateau. The roadside viewpoint and zip-line stop is free to view; the activity is charged.

places.name: Shillong Jadoh and Local Khasi Food
places.description: Jadoh (red rice cooked with pork) is the signature dish of Khasi cuisine. Try also doh-khleh (pork/beef salad with onion and ginger), tungrymbai (fermented soya bean chutney), and boiled vegetables with spiced sauce. Trattoria restaurant and local Khasi eateries in Laitumkhrah are best for authentic food.

places.name: Shillong Cloud 9 — Café Culture
places.description: Shillong is India's rock music capital and has a vibrant café scene. Cloud 9 Café and Dylan's Café are staples for live music evenings, fresh coffee, and Western snacks. The city's unique Khasi-Christian-colonial heritage gives its café culture a distinct character unlike anywhere else in India.
